thread:
erin: Heads-up — opened a TF PR to enable dual-stack IPv6 on our worker VPC and add egress-only gateways for private subnets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4121 :eyes:

Details: enabling `amazon_provided_ipv6_cidr_block` on the VPC, creating `aws_egress_only_internet_gateway` per-AZ, and adding `::/0` routes for private route tables. Also adding a lightweight smoke test job that hits an external IPv6 endpoint.

Quick ask: can folks review the networking bits (routes, module surface, and whether we should BYO vs Amazon-provided IPv6)? Want to canary this in staging next week.

sam: Nice — couple of quick q's: are we allocating IPv6 via AmazonProvided or requesting a BYO from infra? AmazonProvided is fastest but the CIDR might change on VPC re-creation. Also, how does this interact with our existing NAT consolidation plan (we currently rely on NAT GW for IPv4 egress).

erin: Using AmazonProvided for now to keep rollout simple. Agreed NAT GW is IPv4-only; for IPv6 egress we will use `aws_egress_only_internet_gateway` (EIGW) since NAT64 isn't in our plan. Terraform snippet in the PR:```hcl
resource "aws_egress_only_internet_gateway" "eogw" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id
  tags = { Name = "eogw-${var.env}" }
}

resource "aws_route" "private_ipv6_default" {
  for_each = toset(var.private_route_table_ids)
  route_table_id = each.value
  ipv6_cidr_block = "::/0"
  egress_only_internet_gateway_id = aws_egress_only_internet_gateway.eogw.id
}
```

Plan summary from our ci/terraform-runner: "Plan: 6 to add, 3 to change, 0 to destroy" — mostly EIGWs, route entries, and vpc attribute to enable IPv6.

matt: Heads-up for k8s folks: kube-proxy + CNI need dual-stack enabled. Our k8s module toggles `service_ipv6_cidr` and kube-proxy mode; we should add a canary cluster or at least a cordon plan for some worker pools. Also ensure argo rollout jobs target the staging cluster only for tests.

olivia: Re: PrivateLink — I checked: endpoint services in our region don't carry IPv6 to the endpoint ENIs today (NLB can be dual-stack but some endpoint service integrations still prefer IPv4). For internal S3 access we should keep the existing VPC Gateway endpoint (IPv4) and let IPv6 clients use EIGW/egress path. So we need no change to current PrivateLink S3 design.

sam: Good call. One more: we should avoid exposing any public IPv6 addresses on worker nodes by default. Use `assign_ipv6_address_on_creation = false` on subnets and control assignment via ENI settings, then explicitly enable only for canary nodes.

erin: Agreed — in the PR I set `assign_ipv6_address_on_creation = false` for private subnets and left `true` on public subnets. Canary plan: enable IPv6 in staging VPC only, run smoke job that does `curl -6 https://ipv6.test-ipv6.com/` from a canary pod, validate egress and DNS. If green, roll to prod with a maintenance window.

terraform-bot: ci/terraform-runner — plan complete for branch `feature/ipv6-dualstack`: 6 to add, 3 to change, 0 to destroy. Diff includes: +aws_vpc.ipv6_association, +aws_egress_only_internet_gateway.eogw, +aws_route.private_ipv6_default (for each private RT).

matt: I can review the TF module changes later today. @erin please add a short checklist in the PR description for k8s changes + smoke test commands. I'll leave an approval once checklist looks reasonable. :thumbsup:

erin: Will do — added checklist and test commands. Thanks! :rocket:

sam: One small ops note — update the runbook to include troubleshooting steps for IPv6 egress (check `aws ec2 describe-egress-only-internet-gateways`, verify route table entries, and curl via `-6`). I'll draft a one-pager after this merges.

olivia: Also ensure KMS keys and VPC endpoints used by the cluster control plane are accessible over IPv4 still; we don't want control plane traffic to accidentally try IPv6 to endpoints that don't support it.

erin: Good catch — will add that to the checklist. Targeting staging canary next Tue. Thanks everyone for quick reviews!
